newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's cabinet approves budget cut.
newsitem.headline: Israel's cabinet approves budget cut.

text.p: The Israeli cabinet approved a further 1.2 billion shekel budget cut which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said was needed to put the economy back on track and maintain Israel's financial position abroad, officials said.
The government voted 14-4 at the end of an eight-hour session to approve the package, the officials said.
The 1.2 billion shekel cut comes on top of the 4.9 billion shekels of cutbacks included in the original 1997 budget of 190.8 billion shekels.

On the eve of the cabinet session, Treasury sources had put the extra cuts at some 1.8 billion shekels but Netanyahu said before the vote that Finance Minister Dan Meridor had found ways of raising some 600 million shekels without increasing taxes.
"If we don't cut, let there be no doubt that we will pay with a deterioration in our standing in the financial markets and in our credit rating," a statement quoted Netanyahu as telling the cabinet.
"We are presenting another cut because it became clear to us that revenues have not met our expectations," Meridor told Israel Radio.
"Today, the world is watching us -- investors, banks and governments -- to see...whether the government will fix what has gone wrong in the economy in the last two years," he said.
Economists said government revenues have fallen below projections and the prospect of increased government borrowing has pushed up interest rates, strengthened the shekel and sucked in imports.
As a result Israel's current account deficit is expected to widen to more than $5 billion this year from $4.1 billion in 1995.
